newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Home Centers seeks 25 pct profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Home Centers seeks 25 pct profit growth.

text.p: Home Centers (DIY) Ltd, Israel's leading home improvement chain, plans to achieve 25 percent annual growth in net profit through the year 2000, president and chief executive Aharon Meidan said on Thursday.
"My plan is to have each year growth of 25 percent in net profit and earnings per share to the year 2000," Meidan told Reuters in an interview. "This is high-tech growth in a low-tech industry."

Last year the retailer, which went public on Nasdaq in December 1995, earned $2.1 million or $0.43 a share. In 1995, the company did not pay income tax but its earnings would have totalled $0.39 a share on a fully taxed basis.
Revenues in 1996 rose 20.3 percent to $83.9 million.
Home Centers is styled after American warehouse home improvement centers like Home Depot.
The four-year-old company is expanding rapidly, benefiting from a population boom and growing demand for housing and do-it- yourself home improvement.
The company has 10 retail operations and plans to add four more this year, including a 4,000 square meter (43,000 square feet) store next week.

Another four to five stores will be added in 1998 and five Home Centers is also expanding its existing shops and growing vertically by developing stores within its stores. It is starting with a home textiles supermarket based on the concept of the American "Bed, Bath and Beyond".
"It is a very unique concept where we have 60 bedrooms of textiles," Meidan said.

Home Centers has also set its sights on the regional market. It is finalising a 50-50 joint venture agreement with a partner in Cyprus to open at least three stores there for a total investment of $5 million.

It plans, along with Israeli conglomerate Koor Industries and retailer Blue Square Israel, which owns 15.5 percent of Home Centers, to open a shopping mall in Amman, Jordan. "This is still in the planning process," Meidan said.
"We are working hard to find partners in Turkey and Greece as well," he added.

Expansion in Jordan and elsewhere in the region hinges on continuation of the Middle East peace process, Meidan said. "All of us (Koor, Blue Square and Home Centers) believe peace will prevail," Meidan said.
For the domestic market, Home Centers is exploring other marketing niches such as a large nursery based on the European "Garden Center".
Home Centers has a market capitalisation of $28.2 million. Though Nasdaq has become the preferred market for Israeli high-tech issues, an Israeli retailer there is a rarity.
"We felt our kind of business was more suited for the American commmunity. We see big success in our industry for such companies as Home Depot," Meidan said.

"Also, we try to compare ourselves to world leaders in our area in terms of service, management, sales per square foot. We think our management structure will take a step up if we have to work to please Nasdaq. The moment you're there you have to be much better," he said.
Home Centers' shares are trading at $5-1/2, off a 52-week high of $7-5/8. Meidan said the current price does not reflect the shares' true value.
The shares "should be trading at a multiple of 14, and they are now at eight or nine. They are attractive to buy," he said.
